name: Mary, Mother of God
history: On the octave day of Christmas the Church honours Mary under her greatest title, Theotokos, she who gave birth to God. The Council of Ephesus defended the title in 431 because it guards the truth about her Son: the child born of Mary is one Person, true God and true man. Since 1968 the day has also been kept as the World Day of Peace.
life: From the earliest centuries Christians called Mary Theotokos. When Nestorius, archbishop of Constantinople, taught that she should be called only the mother of Christ, the faithful of his own city protested, and in 431 the Council of Ephesus, led by Saint Cyril of Alexandria, upheld the ancient title. The story is told that the people of Ephesus escorted the bishops home with torches. In Rome the first day of January had long been kept with a Marian character. Pius XI instituted a feast of the Divine Motherhood in 1931, on the fifteen-hundredth anniversary of Ephesus, and the reform of the calendar in 1969 placed it here, on the octave of Christmas. The Gospel of the day ends with the shepherds gone and Mary keeping all these things, pondering them in her heart.
prayerTo: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you carried the Word made flesh and gave Him to the world. At the beginning of this year I place my days in your hands. Keep me close to your Son, teach me to ponder His ways in my heart as you did, and pray for peace in our homes and among the nations. Amen.
prayer: We fly to thy patronage, O holy Mother of God; despise not our petitions in our necessities, but deliver us always from all dangers, O glorious and blessed Virgin. Amen.
prayerSource: Sub tuum praesidium, the oldest known prayer to Our Lady
penance: Begin the year with a work of mercy: give to a charity that supports mothers and babies in need, and pray one Hail Mary for peace each day this week.
meditation: Mary kept all these things, pondering them in her heart. Before the year runs away with you, sit for five minutes and ask what God has been saying to you.
